preview_en:
Defending Ligue 1 champions PSG are in the midst of a laboured start to the campaign, but would love to finally put their best foot forward in Le Classique against Marseille .

Match News and Current Form

Marseille opened their campaign in scintillating fashion, but things have quickly soured since as they’ve lost their last three league games. Their woes deepened in midweek when they were thumped 4-1 by Beşiktaş in their UEFA Europa League opener, and boss Bruno Génésio, who only took over in the summer, could be under a huge amount of pressure if they lose here too as it would mark the first time in history that Marseille would have lost four of their opening five Ligue 1 games. They can perhaps seek comfort in the fact April 2015 was the last time they lost four top-flight games in a row, but with that negative streak including a defeat against PSG, they’ll have to be firmly on their guard here.

PSG have made an uncharacteristically poor start to the Ligue 1 season (W1, D2, L1), their worst since the arrival of QSI in 2011/12 and one which has already left them five points off the summit pre-round. While they’ll feel their formidable record in this league is enough to see that gap easily clawed back, they’ll want to avoid seeing it grow this weekend, and hitting the road could provide a good opportunity to do so having won five of their last eight away league games (D2, L1). Adding to that tally here seems highly probable for a PSG side who’ve won 18 of their last 23 Sunday-held Ligue 1 away games (D4, L1), a run which includes three victories to nil on this ground!

Head-to-Head History

Marseille have lost 38 competitive matches against PSG in the 21st century (W13, D12), 15 more than against any other opponent. Struggles have been most evident at home too, where they’ve won just one of the last 13 Ligue 1 H2Hs (D3, L9), although that was the most recent one.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Fourteen of Marseille’s last 18 competitive games produced 4+ total yellow cards.

Since his Ligue 1 debut as a manager in January 2016, Génésio has collected six wins against PSG, at least two more than any other manager.

PSG have only kept one clean sheet in their seven competitive matches this term.

PSG have been caught offside a pre-round league-high 13 times this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Marseille could lean on Igor Paixão after the break given that seven of his last eight club goals came in the second half, the last three of which came at home. PSG summer recruit Maghnes Akliouche has scored a joint-career high three goals against Marseille, and although he’s yet to open his account for his new club, five of his last six strikes for club or country came in away games.

Marseille remain without Geoffrey Kondogbia but hope to have Tochukwu Nnadi available again here. PSG could be without Achraf Hakimi after his early withdrawal last weekend.

Betting Analysis

With Marseille spiralling downwards but still posing an attacking threat at home, backing PSG to win and both teams to score could be the best value pick.

Author: Chris Wilson
